intro: Words for maybe. The expression and the speaker's degree of certainty influence the mood.
p.quizá.nota: Also written quizás; pronunciation varies between seseo and distinción.
p.puede que.nota: In this possibility pattern, use the subjunctive: puede que venga.
p.igual.nota: Colloquial in Spain, with the indicative.
b1.texto:
These expressions normally use the indicative: **a lo mejor**, **igual** (colloquial in Spain), **seguro que**, **supongo que**.

- **A lo mejor** me **quedo** en casa.

Expressions such as **puede (ser) que**, **es posible que** and **es probable que** use the subjunctive: **Puede que nieve**.

With **quizá(s)** and **tal vez**, either mood is possible: **Quizá viene / venga** mañana. **Probablemente**, **posiblemente** and **seguramente** can also take the indicative or present subjunctive: **Seguramente está / esté** en casa. The speaker's degree of certainty can influence the choice, but context and regional usage also matter.

When **no sé si** means ‘I don't know whether’, the indicative is usual in Spain and many other varieties: **No sé si viene** mañana. Some varieties, including Mexican, Caribbean and Andean Spanish, also use the subjunctive here. The accent distinguishes **si** (‘whether’) from **sí** (‘yes’).
b3.f0: Are you coming to the mountains on Saturday?
b3.f1: I don't know if I can. I may have to work.
b3.f2: It may snow. It's likely to be very cold.
b3.f3: Then maybe I'll stay at home.
b3.f4: I'm sure you'll come in the end.
b5.o0.refuerzo: In this possibility pattern, use the subjunctive.
b5.o2.refuerzo: Use the subjunctive with puede que: llueva.
b6.pregunta: Complete: maybe I'll stay at home.
b6.o0.refuerzo: A lo mejor normally uses the indicative: me quedo.
b6.o1.refuerzo: The usual pattern after a lo mejor is indicative: me quedo.
b6.o2.refuerzo: The subject is yo, so use the conjugated present me quedo.
b7.pregunta: Complete: I don't know if he is coming.
b7.o0.refuerzo: The indicative is the usual neutral choice here; some varieties also use the subjunctive.
b7.o1.refuerzo: The indicative is the usual neutral choice here; some varieties also use the subjunctive.
b7.o2.refuerzo: Venir would mean whether I should come.
b8.pregunta: Which one can take either mood?
b8.o0.refuerzo: Tal vez viene and tal vez venga are both possible.
b9.traduccion: I may have to work on Saturday.
b10.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (100–120 words).** Write about your plans for the summer when nothing is certain yet: quizá, a lo mejor, puede que, es probable que.

**Speak (about 2 minutes).** Speculate aloud about what you will be doing in five years.
